title: POC Weekly Sync - Redwood Private upgrade rehearsal prep
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on the upcoming Redwood Private upgrade rehearsal in Harborview’s VPC staging environment. Redwood team reviewed precheck output (Kubernetes version OK, storage class detection still flaky in one cluster context, disk space threshold warning, and missing snapshot IAM permissions for PV snapshots). Customer raised concerns about backup duration (control-plane DB snapshot + verification took ~22–28 minutes in prior dry run) and whether the maintenance window can stay under 60 minutes. Agreed to scope rehearsal to control-plane DB + config/state backup first, with PV snapshots optional/feature-flagged, and to run a timed end-to-end rehearsal with monitoring and a rollback drill. Next steps include updating IAM policy, rerunning prechecks with JSON output for Support, and scheduling a 90-minute rehearsal window with a go/no-go checklist.
topics: POC status update and timeline to upgrade rehearsal
Installer prechecks findings (k8s version, storage class, disk, permissions)
Backup step performance (DB snapshot + verify) and maintenance window
Snapshot/IAM permissions for backups in VPC
Rollback guardrails and what is/isn’t supported for forward-only migrations
Observability during upgrade (correlation id, logs, dashboards)
Rehearsal plan: go/no-go, smoke tests, rollback drill
questions: Can we skip PV snapshots for the rehearsal and still meet Redwood’s recommended safety bar?
If the DB migration is marked forward-only, what does rollback do (stop + restore) vs blocking?
What signals should we watch to call go/no-go during the upgrade (specific dashboards/alerts)?
Can Redwood provide a non-interactive mode for rollback so we can run it in automation?
action_items: Harborview (Tom) - Add/confirm IAM permissions for EBS snapshot + describe/list for installer backup step; share policy diff with Redwood - due 2025-01-20
Redwood (Devon) - Send exact precheck remediation notes for storage class detection and disk space threshold; include command examples - due 2025-01-17
Redwood (Rafael) - Share the upgrade runbook section for timed rehearsal (what to monitor, stop conditions, rollback steps) - due 2025-01-17
Harborview (Priya) - Reserve a 90-minute staging maintenance window for the rehearsal; propose 2 options - due 2025-01-21
Redwood (Connor) - Confirm which private release build + chart versions Harborview should pin for the rehearsal and provide bundle checksums - due 2025-01-20
Harborview (Lena) - Confirm whether PV snapshots are allowed under internal policy, or must be disabled; provide decision - due 2025-01-21
next_steps: Rerun prechecks with updated IAM permissions and share JSON output + diagnostics bundle
Agree on rehearsal scope (DB + config backup required; PV snapshots optional) and success criteria (timing, health checks, rollback drill)
Schedule upgrade rehearsal with Redwood on bridge + screen share; use go/no-go checklist
After rehearsal, capture timings and any failures and turn into a GA readiness delta list
transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Meeting: POC Weekly Sync - Redwood Private upgrade rehearsal prep
Recorded: 2025-01-16 17:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes

Attendees
Redwood Inference: Markus Klein, Rafael Mendes, Devon Price, Connor O'Brien
Harborview Analytics: Priya Desai, Tom Wheeler, Lena Park, Miguel Santos

---
Summary (auto-generated)
- Reviewed POC progress and readiness for Private upgrade rehearsal in staging.
- Discussed precheck findings: storage class detection issue, disk space warning, and missing snapshot permissions.
- Discussed backup timing concerns and proposed scoping PV snapshots as optional.
- Aligned on next steps and scheduling.

Topics (auto-generated)
1) Precheck results
2) Backup/restore timing
3) Rollback policy and guardrails
4) Rehearsal plan + go/no-go

Action Items (auto-generated)
- Harborview to update IAM for snapshots
- Redwood to send runbook + monitoring checklist
- Schedule rehearsal window

---

[00:00] Markus Klein: Alright, cool. I think we’re live. Thanks everybody for joining. This is the weekly POC sync, mostly focused today on the upgrade rehearsal prep. Quick roll call—Priya, Tom, Lena, Miguel, you’re all on?

[00:11] Priya Desai: Yep, I’m here.

[00:12] Tom Wheeler: Here.

[00:13] Lena Park: Yep.

[00:14] Miguel Santos: On.

[00:16] Markus Klein: Great. From Redwood we’ve got Rafa, Devon, and Connor. Connor’s here specifically for version pinning and release bits. Goal today: (1) status, (2) precheck findings, (3) backup duration and maintenance window, and then we lock next steps + time for rehearsal.

[00:37] Rafael Mendes: Hey all.

[00:38] Devon Price: Hi.

[00:39] Connor O'Brien: Hey.

[00:42] Markus Klein: Priya, do you want to start with where you’re at on staging? Like, are we still targeting next week?

[00:49] Priya Desai: Yeah, I think so. Staging is in good shape. We rolled out the latest Redwood Private control plane build you gave us—well, “latest” from last week. Runtime pods look stable. The only thing is the precheck output, we got a couple reds that we need to resolve.

[01:08] Markus Klein: Perfect. Devon, do you want to pull up what we saw in the precheck?

[01:12] Devon Price: Yeah. So, the report you sent—thank you for that—had: Kubernetes version check passed, node count passed, CPU/mem headroom passed. Storage class detection… it flagged “no default storage class” but I think it’s a false positive based on context or the API it’s using.

[01:31] Tom Wheeler: That’s what we thought. We do have a default set. It’s gp3.

[01:35] Devon Price: Right. I’ve seen this when the cluster has multiple storage classes and the annotation isn’t readable under the service account the installer is using. The installer is doing a list + get and looking for the annotation `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class=true`.

[01:53] Lena Park: That might be RBAC. We constrained the service account pretty hard.

[01:56] Devon Price: That would do it. It’ll read as “not found” and we currently show it as “no default.” We’re tightening the messaging, but for now the fix is either grant get/list on storageclasses, or pass an override flag to the installer config to point at the storage class explicitly.

[02:14] Priya Desai: Prefer the override, honestly.

[02:16] Devon Price: Totally fine. We can do that for the rehearsal.

[02:20] Markus Klein: The other big precheck was disk space, right?

[02:23] Priya Desai: Yeah. It says like, “/var/lib/containerd below 15% free.” But we’re not actually that low. We’re around 22-ish.

[02:31] Tom Wheeler: It might be measuring a different mount point. We have separate volumes.

[02:35] Devon Price: Exactly. It’s measuring the node filesystem where the installer runs the check—if it’s using `kubectl debug` it might see the host mount differently depending on the distro. That one is a warning-level check, not a hard stop.

[02:49] Rafael Mendes: For the rehearsal, we’ll treat it as yellow unless it’s truly below the threshold. But we should validate because upgrades do spike image pulls, and then you also generate the diagnostics bundle.

[03:03] Miguel Santos: The diagnostics bundle is like tarball of logs, right?

[03:05] Rafael Mendes: Yeah, it grabs precheck report, step timings, some k8s events, and last N lines of pod logs for key namespaces. It can be a couple hundred megs depending.

[03:16] Markus Klein: The third precheck—this is the one that blocks backups—was snapshot permissions.

[03:22] Tom Wheeler: Yep. It’s saying it can’t create snapshots. We didn’t grant the installer role `ec2:CreateSnapshot` and friends.

[03:31] Lena Park: We need to be careful. Snapshotting volumes touches data governance rules for us. We can do DB snapshot probably, but PV snapshots might be a bigger internal review.

[03:42] Connor O'Brien: Just to clarify: the baseline we’re pushing for is control-plane DB snapshot + verification and backing up config/state from object storage or the internal state bucket. PV snapshots are optional depending on your risk tolerance and policy. But the installer precheck currently assumes it might do PV snapshots if configured.

[04:03] Priya Desai: So can we scope the rehearsal to DB + config backup only, and keep PV snapshots turned off?

[04:09] Rafael Mendes: Yes. We can configure it so the backup step is DB snapshot + verify only. The PV snapshot check would become informational.

[04:16] Markus Klein: That might help with the time window too. Which is the next topic—backup duration. Tom, you mentioned on Slack the dry run took longer than expected.

[04:27] Tom Wheeler: Yeah. We ran the snapshot step in isolation. Control plane Postgres—well, it’s RDS in our VPC—snapshot plus the verification query took about 26 minutes. That’s… not great if our maintenance window is 60.

[04:43] Priya Desai: And that’s before we actually pull images and run migrations and roll pods.

[04:48] Devon Price: Totally fair. The “verification” is essentially: wait for snapshot completion, restore to a temp instance in some modes, or run a basic consistency check if it’s in-place. In your case, because it’s managed, we’re waiting on AWS snapshot completion.

[05:06] Tom Wheeler: It’s waiting on AWS, yeah.

[05:08] Connor O'Brien: The timing is also dependent on volume size and IOPS. For rehearsal, we can capture the exact timings per sub-step, so you have data for your internal change request.

[05:19] Lena Park: But the question is: do you require the snapshot to finish before proceeding? Like can we “start snapshot” and proceed, then validate later?

[05:28] Rafael Mendes: In v1, we’re conservative: backup must be completed and verified before we apply the upgrade. Otherwise you get into a bad place where you’ve mutated state but your recovery point is unknown.

[05:42] Priya Desai: Okay. That means we need a larger window.

[05:45] Markus Klein: Yeah. For beta we’ve been recommending 90 minutes for the first rehearsal, then you can tighten based on the observed timings.

[05:54] Tom Wheeler: 90 might be possible in staging, production will be harder. But okay for rehearsal.

[05:59] Miguel Santos: For production we’ll probably need to do it overnight.

[06:02] Markus Klein: Makes sense.

[06:05] Priya Desai: Can we talk rollback? Because if we take a 90 minute window and something fails, we need to be confident what “rollback” means.

[06:12] Rafael Mendes: Yep. So the rollback command will re-apply previous Helm chart versions and, if the DB migration step hasn’t crossed a forward-only boundary, it can restore the snapshot. If the migration is marked forward-only, the installer should block rollback and instruct you to restore from backup manually—or roll forward.

[06:31] Priya Desai: That’s the part I want crisp. How do we know it’s forward-only?

[06:36] Connor O'Brien: There’s migration metadata that tags a release. The control plane reports it, and the installer checks compatibility and “downgrade-safe” flags. If it’s forward-only, rollback is essentially “abort” not “downgrade.”

[06:52] Lena Park: So rollback might not always bring us to the previous version.

[06:56] Rafael Mendes: Correct. It’s a guardrail to prevent split-brain or data corruption.

[07:02] Tom Wheeler: We need that in the change doc. Like, clearly.

[07:06] Markus Klein: Yep. We’ll send language you can paste into your internal ticket: “Rollback supported only within same schema compatibility window; forward-only migrations block downgrade.”

[07:18] Priya Desai: Good.

[07:20] Devon Price: Also the operator UX: it prints a plan graph—like steps and dependencies—and highlights where rollback-safe boundaries are. The “upgrade plan” is readable, and there’s a `--json` for Support.

[07:35] Miguel Santos: The plan graph is like… a DAG?

[07:37] Devon Price: Yeah, basically. It’s not fancy UI, but it shows ordering: prechecks → backup → apply control plane → migrations gate → gateway rollout → smoke tests.

[07:50] Markus Klein: Let’s zoom in on the specific prechecks we need to clear to be “green” for rehearsal.

[07:56] Devon Price: Snapshot permissions: we need at minimum permission to create the DB snapshot (RDS API) and read status. For PV snapshots, if disabled, we can skip those. For storage class detection, either RBAC for storageclass list/get or override. Disk—validate threshold with your node mounts; if you’re truly above 15% free, we’ll mark it as pass.

[08:20] Tom Wheeler: On IAM, we can do RDS snapshot permissions pretty fast. PV snapshots might take longer. And for EBS you’d need `ec2:CreateSnapshot`, `ec2:CreateTags`, `ec2:Describe*`, probably.

[08:35] Lena Park: And those need to be scoped. Not wildcard.

[08:38] Connor O'Brien: Totally. We’ve got a least-privilege example policy we can share. And for the rehearsal we can keep it to RDS only.

[08:47] Markus Klein: Cool. Let’s talk timing of the rehearsal. Priya, you said next week. What days are possible?

[08:55] Priya Desai: Tuesday or Thursday. But I need to check with the team.

[09:00] Tom Wheeler: Tuesday is better.

[09:02] Markus Klein: Connor, are we in a stable release by Tuesday?

[09:06] Connor O'Brien: I think yes, but I’d rather confirm. We have a private release train cut on Monday. For beta, we want you pinned to the exact versions so we can reproduce issues. I’ll send the versions and checksums.

[09:20] Priya Desai: Great.

[09:22] Rafael Mendes: During rehearsal, I’d like to have you run with a bridge open. We’ll monitor: upgrade step duration metrics, failure counters, and service health—API 200 rates, latency, plus control plane readiness.

[09:37] Tom Wheeler: Do you have dashboards we can import, or is it in your observability pack?

[09:42] Rafael Mendes: If you’re using the observability pack, there are dashboards for upgrade runs. If not, we can provide metric names and you can wire them into Grafana.

[09:52] Miguel Santos: We have Prometheus + Grafana already.

[09:55] Rafael Mendes: Great. The key is correlation id. The installer emits a correlation id, and the control plane logs propagate it. So you can pivot between installer step logs and service logs.

[10:12] Priya Desai: Okay. That’s helpful for debugging.

[10:15] Markus Klein: On the backup duration concern: are we aligned that for rehearsal we accept it may be 25–30 minutes, and we run a 90-minute window?

[10:27] Priya Desai: Yes, for staging.

[10:29] Tom Wheeler: As long as we can measure it.

[10:31] Markus Klein: Yep. And we’ll also capture “where time went.” If it’s all in AWS snapshot completion, then you can decide whether to adjust RDS settings or schedule longer windows.

[10:44] Lena Park: I also want to confirm the backup data is encrypted. Our RDS snapshots are encrypted with our KMS key.

[10:51] Connor O'Brien: Yep, we don’t change that. The snapshot uses your settings. For any config/state artifacts, those remain in your bucket with your encryption settings.

[11:02] Lena Park: Good.

[11:04] Markus Klein: Any other precheck findings? Miguel, you had mentioned schema mismatch once?

[11:10] Miguel Santos: Not mismatch, but we saw a warning about “db extension version.” It said something about pgcrypto.

[11:17] Devon Price: That’s a soft check. It just validates required extensions exist. If it’s warning, it might not have permission to query `pg_available_extensions`. If you can grant read on that, it’ll be clean.

[11:31] Priya Desai: We can do that.

[11:33] Tom Wheeler: Wait, is the installer connecting as the app user?

[11:36] Devon Price: It should use the control plane DB user. If that user is restricted, you’ll see those warnings. It won’t block upgrade unless it’s missing a required extension.

[11:49] Markus Klein: Let’s do a quick recap of the rehearsal success criteria.

[11:54] Rafael Mendes: I’ll propose: (1) prechecks all pass or only known warnings with sign-off; (2) backup completes + verify; (3) upgrade completes with smoke tests passing; (4) capture step timings; (5) perform a rollback drill—either full rollback if safe, or at least run the rollback command in “plan” mode and validate it would block appropriately if forward-only.

[12:19] Priya Desai: I’d like an actual rollback in staging, yes.

[12:22] Tom Wheeler: Same.

[12:24] Connor O'Brien: We can do that as long as the upgrade path does not include forward-only migrations. I’ll verify the migration flags for the target release. If it’s forward-only, we can’t do a downgrade safely.

[12:39] Priya Desai: Understood.

[12:41] Markus Klein: Any concern with running rollback right after upgrade? Like, does it leave anything weird?

[12:47] Rafael Mendes: That’s what the rehearsal is for. In staging, it’s fine. It’s also a good test for the “previous known good version” tracking.

[12:58] Tom Wheeler: Cool.

[13:00] (crosstalk)

[13:01] Miguel Santos: One more thing—during the dry run, the installer output was a little hard to read. It printed a lot of stuff.

[13:08] Devon Price: Yeah, fair. We’ve been tightening it. For you, run with `--json` so you can archive it and we can ingest it. For the human run, we can set it to “compact” mode—less spam.

[13:22] Priya Desai: Great.

[13:24] Markus Klein: Let’s talk about the AWS permissions piece. Tom, what do you need from Redwood to move that forward?

[13:30] Tom Wheeler: A sample policy would help. Also, I want to know exactly which calls the installer makes so we can scope it.

[13:38] Connor O'Brien: For RDS snapshots: `rds:CreateDBSnapshot`, `rds:DescribeDBSnapshots`, `rds:DescribeDBInstances`, and tag permissions if you tag snapshots. For EBS: same idea but we can defer.

[13:54] Lena Park: And we need audit logs of who initiated upgrade.

[13:58] Connor O'Brien: The control plane emits audit events for upgrade/rollback actions—who, when, what version, correlation id.

[14:08] Lena Park: Perfect.

[14:10] Markus Klein: Okay. Scheduling: Priya will propose Tuesday or Thursday. Let’s pencil Tuesday 17:00 UTC same time?

[14:19] Priya Desai: That’s okay for us.

[14:21] Tom Wheeler: Works.

[14:22] Miguel Santos: Works.

[14:23] Lena Park: Works.

[14:25] Markus Klein: Great. We’ll do a 90-minute window. We’ll share a go/no-go checklist before.

[14:31] Rafael Mendes: And I’ll send the monitoring checklist: what dashboards, what to watch. If error rate spikes, we stop. If control plane health doesn’t come back within X minutes, we stop.

[14:43] Priya Desai: Can you define X?

[14:45] Rafael Mendes: For beta, we’ve been using 10 minutes for control plane readiness post-apply, 15 for gateway rollout. But we can tune based on your environment.

[14:57] Tom Wheeler: That’s fine.

[15:00] Markus Klein: Anything else? Competitors—just to sanity check, your internal stakeholders are comparing this to “just use SageMaker endpoints” or something?

[15:09] Priya Desai: Yeah, that comes up. But we need VPC isolation and predictable latency, and their model serving story is… not great for what we do.

[15:18] Markus Klein: Got it.

[15:20] Priya Desai: Also Anyscale came up as an option for self-hosting, but then we’d own the upgrades, which is the pain we’re trying to avoid.

[15:29] Markus Klein: Exactly.

[15:31] (brief pause)

[15:33] Devon Price: One more thing on the storage class check: if you pick the override, I’ll send the exact value you should set. Sometimes folks put the provisioner name, but we need the storage class resource name.

[15:46] Priya Desai: Okay. Send that.

[15:48] Markus Klein: Great. Let’s do final recap and we’ll end early if we can.

[15:54] Markus Klein: Recap: Tom will update IAM for RDS snapshot permissions and share the diff. Devon will send remediation notes for storage class + disk check, plus command examples, and the storage class override value. Rafa sends the timed rehearsal runbook + monitoring checklist. Connor sends pinned versions and checksums for the rehearsal. Priya will propose two time slots and book a 90-minute staging window. Lena will confirm policy on PV snapshots (allowed or disabled).

[16:25] Priya Desai: Sounds right.

[16:26] Tom Wheeler: Yep.

[16:27] Lena Park: Yes.

[16:28] Miguel Santos: Yep.

[16:30] Markus Klein: Cool. Anything else pressing?

[16:34] Tom Wheeler: Not from me.

[16:36] Priya Desai: No.

[16:37] Lena Park: All good.

[16:39] Markus Klein: Great. Thanks everyone. We’ll follow up on email with the action items and tentative Tuesday rehearsal.

[16:46] (meeting ends)
